region: West Africa (Senegal/Mauritania to Lake Chad and northern Cameroon; Sahel, Sahara margins and forest belt)

polities.name: Jolof Empire
polities.note: Overlord of Waalo, Cayor, Baol, Sine and Saloum; broke apart after Battle of Danki (1549). Court mobile within Jolof province.

polities.name: Kingdom of Jolof
polities.note: Landlocked rump of the Jolof Empire after 1549; French occupation 1890 (Alboury Ndiaye fled).

polities.name: Cayor
polities.note: Largest Jolof successor; damels often also ruled Baol (Damel-Teigne). Cap-Vert Lebou broke away 1790s. French annexation 1886; seat precision ~0.1 deg.

polities.name: Baol
polities.note: Frequently in personal union with Cayor (e.g. 1549, 1693-1756); French protectorate/annexation by 1894.

polities.name: Waalo
polities.note: Lower Senegal River delta kingdom around Lac de Guiers; annexed by French Senegal 1855.

polities.name: Lebou Republic
polities.note: Lebou theocratic polity on the Cap-Vert peninsula after seceding from Cayor c.1790-1795; absorbed with French founding of Dakar 1857.

polities.name: Kingdom of Sine
polities.note: Serer kingdom; French protectorate 1891 (traditional monarchy to 1969).

polities.name: Kingdom of Saloum
polities.note: Serer-Wolof kingdom; at height extended to Gambia north bank (tribute from Niumi, Badibu). Seat later Kaolack area. French protectorate 1891.

polities.name: Empire of Great Fulo
polities.note: Founded by Koli Tenguella; core is Futa Toro along the middle Senegal. Hegemony (tribute) over Jolof, Waalo, Gajaaga, Diarra, Saloum in 16th-early 17th c. Overthrown by Torodbe revolution 1776.

polities.name: Imamate of Futa Toro
polities.note: Elective almamate; no fixed capital (almamis resided in own villages). French annexed provinces 1859-1861; remnant resistance to 1890.

polities.name: Gajaaga
polities.note: Soninke kingdom on upper Senegal between Bakel and the Falémé confluence; split into Goye and Kamera in 1830s; French control by 1858.

polities.name: Bundu
polities.note: Fula almamate west of the Falémé; earlier seat Koussan. French treaties from 1845, formal end 1905.

polities.name: Khasso
polities.note: Fula-Malinke kingdom around Kayes on the upper Senegal; fragmented in 19th c; French fort at Medine 1855, protectorate by 1880.

polities.name: Bambouk
polities.note: Gold-bearing Malinke chiefdoms between Falémé and Bafing; no single ruler. Fill area rather than state.

polities.name: Kingdom of Diarra
polities.note: Soninke successor kingdom in the Kingi/Nioro region; conquered by Kaarta Bambara 1754.

polities.name: Kingdom of Niumi
polities.note: Mandinka kingdom on the north bank of the Gambia mouth; ceded Ceded Mile to Britain 1826, protectorate 1897.

polities.name: Badibu
polities.note: Mandinka kingdom on Gambia north bank east of Niumi; Islamic state of Ma Ba Diakhou (Rip) 1861-1867. British protectorate 1897.

polities.name: Kingdom of Wuli
polities.note: Mandinka kingdom on the upper Gambia north bank, east of Kantora and Niani; British protectorate 1898.

polities.name: Kiang
polities.note: Mandinka kingdom on Gambia south bank, tributary to Kaabu; British protectorate 1894.

polities.name: Kombo
polities.note: Mandinka kingdom at the Gambia mouth south bank; British Kombo cessions 1840-1855, Soninke-Marabout wars, protectorate 1894.

polities.name: Kaabu
polities.note: Mali's western province, independent 1537; federation of provinces from Gambia River to Futa Jallon foothills. Kansala fell to Futa Jallon 1867. Kansala seat approximate (~0.15 deg).

polities.name: Fuladu
polities.note: Fula kingdom of Alfa Molo and Musa Molo in upper Casamance, carved from Kaabu; partitioned by British, French and Portuguese 1903.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bissau
polities.note: Papel chiefdom on Bissau island coexisting with Portuguese fort (from 1687); subdued by Portugal 1915.

polities.name: Emirate of Trarza
polities.note: Hassaniya Arab (Awlad Ahmad bin Daman) emirate of SW Mauritania; nomadic court; gum trade with Saint-Louis. French protectorate 1902.

polities.name: Emirate of Brakna
polities.note: Hassani emirate north of the middle Senegal; nomadic court. French protectorate 1903.

polities.name: Emirate of Tagant
polities.note: Idaw'ish (Zenaga-origin) emirate on the Tagant plateau; emirate formalised 18th c. French conquest 1905 (Coppolani killed at Tidjikja).

polities.name: Emirate of Adrar
polities.note: Hassani (Yahya ben Uthman) emirate around Atar, Chinguetti and Ouadane; French conquest 1909.

polities.name: Hodh Hassani tribes
polities.note: Awlad Mbarak dominant 17th-18th c., displaced by Mashduf in 19th c.; Oualata a scholarly town. Use as fill for the Hodh.

polities.name: Imamate of Futa Jallon
polities.note: Fula almamate of the Guinea highlands; religious capital Fugumba. Nine provinces (diwe). French protectorate 1881 (nominal), occupation 1896.

polities.name: Baté Empire
polities.note: Maninka Muslim (Kaba clan) state around Kankan on the Milo; taken over by Samori 1881, French 1891.

polities.name: Solima
polities.note: Yalunka kingdom on the upper Niger/Rokel watershed (NE Sierra Leone); long war with Futa Jallon; Falaba destroyed by Samori's forces 1884.

polities.name: Moria
polities.note: Muslim Manika/Susu state on the Guinea coast between Melakori and Scarcies rivers; absorbed into French Guinea c.1890.

polities.name: Koya Temne
polities.note: Temne kingdom inland of the Sierra Leone estuary; ceded the Freetown peninsula (1788/1807). British protectorate 1896.

polities.name: Sherbro chiefdoms
polities.note: Sherbro (Bullom) chiefdoms of the southern Sierra Leone coast, with Afro-European Caulker and Tucker trading lineages; Sherbro Island ceded to Britain 1861-62, protectorate 1896.

polities.name: Kpaa Mende Confederacy
polities.note: Mende war-chief confederacy in south-central Sierra Leone; under Madam Yoko (Senehun) 1878-1906 an ally of Britain. Other Mende chiefdoms (Luawa, Bumpe) lie east and south.

polities.name: Gallinas
polities.note: Vai chiefdoms of the Gallinas River (Massaquoi dynasty), major slave-trade centre to 1850; partitioned between Sierra Leone and Liberia 1885-1890.

polities.name: Condo Confederation
polities.note: Mandingo/Gola/Vai trade confederation in NW Liberia under Sao Boso and successors; fragmented after 1840s and absorbed by Liberia.

polities.name: Grebo confederation
polities.note: Grebo town confederations of the far SE Liberian coast; repeated wars with Maryland/Liberia (1857, 1875, 1910).

polities.name: Kru Coast towns
polities.note: Autonomous Kru 'dako' town confederations of the SE Liberian coast; nominally Liberian after 1847. Fill with low confidence.

polities.name: Liberia
polities.note: ACS colony 1822, independent 1847, absorbed Maryland 1857. Effective control was a coastal strip ~40-60 km deep; the interior stayed under indigenous chiefdoms to c.1900.

polities.name: Republic of Maryland
polities.note: Maryland State Colonization Society settlement at Cape Palmas; independent 1854, annexed by Liberia 1857.

polities.name: Sierra Leone Colony
polities.note: Freetown peninsula colony (Sierra Leone Company 1792, Crown 1808); hinterland protectorate 1896 covers all modern Sierra Leone.

polities.name: Wassoulou Empire
polities.note: Samori Toure's state; driven east by the French 1891-94 into northern Cote d'Ivoire/Ghana (Kong destroyed 1897); Samori captured 1898. Bissandugu seat approx.

polities.name: Kénédougou Kingdom
polities.note: Senufo-Dyula kingdom; extent shown at peak under Tieba and Babemba (1870s-1890s), earlier smaller. French took Sikasso 1898.

polities.name: Mali Empire
polities.note: Lost Timbuktu (1433) and the Sahel to Tuareg/Songhai, Djenné c.1473; Gambia/Kaabu provinces lost 1537; defeated at Djenné 1599 and broke up c.1670 after Bamana attacks. Late capitals uncertain.

polities.name: Kangaba
polities.note: Keita rump of Mali in the Manden heartland on the upper Niger; French control 1888.

polities.name: Songhai Empire
polities.note: Expansion under Sunni Ali (1464-92) and Askia Muhammad; Agadez and Hausa states (Katsina, Kano) paid tribute in the 16th c. (not drawn). Fell to Morocco at Tondibi 1591.

polities.name: Dendi Kingdom
polities.note: Askia remnant of Songhai in the lower Niger valley after 1591; larger in early 17th c., later fragmented into small Songhai/Zarma chiefdoms (Tera, Anzourou, Gorouol). French deposed last askia 1901.

polities.name: Pashalik of Timbuktu
polities.note: Moroccan conquest state ruled by Arma pashas; after c.1660 shrank to Timbuktu, Gao and Djenné towns (reach_km applies to 1660-1833).

polities.name: Fula Kingdom of Massina
polities.note: Fula pastoral kingdom of the Ardo (Dialloube) dynasty in the inner Niger delta; overthrown by Seku Amadu 1818.

polities.name: Massina Empire
polities.note: Fula jihad state of Seku Amadu in the inner Niger delta; held Timbuktu 1826-1844. Conquered by Umar Tall 1862.

polities.name: Bamana Empire
polities.note: Founded by Biton Coulibaly, Ngolo Diarra dynasty from 1766; took Djenné and Massina; conquered by Umar Tall 1861.

polities.name: Kaarta
polities.note: Massassi Coulibaly kingdom; pushed west by Ségou in 1754 and conquered Diarra; vassals Khasso and Bambuk raids. Taken by Umar Tall 1854.

polities.name: Toucouleur Empire
polities.note: Umar Tall's jihad state; after 1864 divided between Ahmadu (Ségou/Nioro) and Tijani (Bandiagara/Massina). French took Ségou 1890, Nioro 1891, Bandiagara 1893.

polities.name: Kong Empire
polities.note: Dyula (Wattara) trading state in NE Cote d'Ivoire; Gwiriko broke away 1740. Kong destroyed by Samori 1897, French 1898.

polities.name: Gwiriko
polities.note: Wattara kingdom on the Mouhoun bend incl. Tiefo, Dafin and Bwamu areas; French occupation 1897.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bouna
polities.note: Kulango kingdom founded by a Dagomba-derived dynasty in the 17th c.; destroyed by Samori 1896.

polities.name: Gyaman
polities.note: Abron (Bono-Akan) kingdom straddling the Cote d'Ivoire-Ghana border; split between French and British spheres 1897.

polities.name: Gonja
polities.note: Founded by Mande cavalry under Sumaila Ndewura Jakpa (trad. c.1550-1675); divisional chiefdoms incl. Kpembe (Salaga), Bole, Buipe. British protectorate 1899 (eastern part briefly German).

polities.name: Kingdom of Dagbon
polities.note: Moved its capital east to Yendi c.1700 after Gonja pressure; partitioned between German Togo (Yendi) and British Gold Coast 1899.

polities.name: Mamprugu
polities.note: Senior Mole-Dagbani kingdom, parent of the Mossi dynasties; British protectorate 1898.

polities.name: Nanung
polities.note: Small Mole-Dagbani kingdom south-east of Dagbon; German Togo/British partition 1899.

polities.name: Kingdom of Wala
polities.note: Mole-Dagbani dynasty with Muslim Dyula community in NW Ghana; raided by Babatu and Samori, British 1896.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ouagadougou
polities.note: Paramount Mossi kingdom of the Mogho Naba (capital fixed at Ouagadougou c.1681); French occupation 1896.

polities.name: Kingdom of Yatenga
polities.note: Northern Mossi kingdom; Ouahigouya founded as capital 1757 by Naba Kango. French protectorate 1895.

polities.name: Kingdom of Tenkodogo
polities.note: Oldest Mossi kingdom (traditional founding 12th c.), in SE Burkina Faso; French 1897.

polities.name: Kingdom of Boussouma
polities.note: Semi-independent Mossi kingdom NE of Ouagadougou (also Riziam, Mané, Kaya chiefdoms nearby, not itemised).

polities.name: Nungu
polities.note: Paramount Gurma kingdom of eastern Burkina Faso; other Gurma chiefdoms (Pama, Kpatchari) under loose suzerainty. French 1895.

polities.name: Liptako Emirate
polities.note: Fula jihad emirate replacing Gurma rule in NE Burkina Faso; French 1897.

polities.name: Dosso Kingdom
polities.note: Zarma kingdom in SW Niger; resisted Sokoto/Gwandu raids; allied with France 1898. Other Zarma chiefdoms (Zarmaganda) not itemised.

polities.name: Kel Ahaggar
polities.note: Tuareg confederation of the Ahaggar massif under an amenokal (Kel Ghela); French victory at Tit 1902, submission 1905.

polities.name: Kel Ajjer
polities.note: Tuareg confederation of the Tassili n'Ajjer around Ghat and Djanet; French at Djanet 1911, Italians at Ghat 1913.

polities.name: Sultanate of Agadez
polities.note: Sultan at Agadez arbitrated among Air Tuareg confederations (Kel Ewey, Kel Fadey, Kel Gres before migration). French occupation 1900-1906.

polities.name: Iwellemmeden Kel Ataram
polities.note: Western Iwellemmeden around Ménaka and the Gao Niger bend; until c.1770 one confederacy with Kel Dinnik. Dominated Timbuktu/Gao region in 18th-19th c.; revolt of Firhun crushed 1916.

polities.name: Iwellemmeden Kel Dinnik
polities.note: Eastern Iwellemmeden of the Azawagh and Tahoua region; in conflict with Sokoto and Adar; Kaocen/Tuareg revolt 1916-17.

polities.name: Kel Adagh
polities.note: Ifoghas-led confederation of the Adrar des Ifoghas; tributary to the Kel Ataram for much of the 19th c.

polities.name: Kel Tademaket
polities.note: Tuareg confederation of the Timbuktu-Goundam lakes region; dominated Timbuktu 18th c. (sack 1737); French at Timbuktu 1894. Kel Antessar and Arab Berabich/Kunta also present.

polities.name: Kel Gres
polities.note: Tuareg group that migrated from Air to the Gobir/Ader borderlands in the 18th c.; tributary relations with Gobir and Sokoto.

polities.name: Asante Empire
polities.note: Peak extent (1745-1874) includes tributary Gonja, Dagbon, Gyaman, Bono, Akyem; directly ruled metropolitan core much smaller. Lost the south after 1874; British occupation 1896, annexation 1901.

polities.name: Bono State
polities.note: Early Akan gold-trading kingdom near Techiman; conquered by Asante 1723 (Techiman later reconstituted as Asante tributary).

polities.name: Denkyira
polities.note: Dominant Akan power of the 17th c. (Adansi, Assin, Wassa, Aowin, early Asante as vassals); defeated by Asante at Feyiase 1701. Moved south to Jukwa after 1824; British protectorate 1874.

polities.name: Akwamu
polities.note: Conquered Ga (Accra) 1677-81, Ladoku, and Ewe coastlands to Whydah's border; overthrown by Akyem 1730 and resettled on the Volta at Akwamufie. British protectorate 1874.

polities.name: Fante states
polities.note: Coastal Akan states (Mankessim, Anomabu, Abora, Ekumfi, Gomoa) that absorbed Fetu/Eguafo areas in the 18th c.; formal Fante Confederation 1868-1872; Gold Coast Colony 1874.

polities.name: Ga Kingdom
polities.note: Ga kingdom of the Accra plains; conquered by Akwamu 1677-1681. Coastal Ga towns (Ga Mashie, Osu, La) continued around European forts under Akwamu, Akyem and Asante influence.

polities.name: Akyem Abuakwa
polities.note: Largest Akyem state; defeated Akwamu 1730 and briefly held Accra. British protectorate 1874.

polities.name: Akyem Kotoku
polities.note: Akyem state west of Abuakwa; seat at Gyadam until mid-19th c., then Oda.

polities.name: Akuapem
polities.note: State formed on the Akuapem ridge after the fall of Akwamu (1733), Akyem-derived dynasty; British protectorate 1874.

polities.name: Kwahu
polities.note: Akan state on the Kwahu plateau; left Asante for British protection 1874-1888.

polities.name: Adansi
polities.note: Early Akan state south of Kumasi; Treaty of Fomena 1874 signed here; fled into British territory 1886.

polities.name: Kingdom of Assin
polities.note: Akan chiefdoms between Denkyira and the Fante coast on the Kumasi-Cape Coast road; British protectorate 1874.

polities.name: Wassa
polities.note: Gold-rich Akan state (later split Fiase/Amenfi) in SW Ghana behind Ahanta; British protectorate 1874.

polities.name: Sefwi
polities.note: Akan forest states (Wiawso, Anhwiaso, Bekwai) in western Ghana; Asante tributary.

polities.name: Aowin
polities.note: Akan kingdom of the far west Gold Coast forest; many Aowin migrated to found Sanwi (Cote d'Ivoire) in the 18th c.

polities.name: Nzema (Apollonia)
polities.note: Nzema coastal kingdom(s) around Beyin and Atuabo; strong under Kaku Aka in the 1840s; British 1874.

polities.name: Ahanta
polities.note: Coastal Akan kingdom around Busua, Dixcove and Takoradi; Dutch Ahanta war 1837-38.

polities.name: Fetu Kingdom
polities.note: Coastal kingdom behind Cape Coast; absorbed into the Fante sphere in the early 18th c.

polities.name: Eguafo
polities.note: Coastal kingdom including Elmina and Komenda; Komenda Wars 1694-1700; declined in the 18th c. (Elmina became autonomous under the Dutch).

polities.name: Anlo
polities.note: Ewe state on the Keta lagoon coast; British annexation of the coast 1874-1879.

polities.name: Kingdom of Sanwi
polities.note: Anyi (Agni) kingdom founded by Aowin emigrants on the Aby lagoon; French treaty 1843, part of Cote d'Ivoire 1893.

polities.name: Indénié
polities.note: Anyi kingdom of eastern Cote d'Ivoire; French protectorate treaties 1887-1893.

polities.name: Baoulé chiefdoms
polities.note: Baoulé Akan migrants under Queen Abla Pokou (c.1730) formed loosely-federated chiefdoms (Warebo at Sakassou paramount); resisted French until c.1911.

polities.name: Notsé
polities.note: Walled Ewe kingdom; tyranny of Agokoli caused the Ewe dispersal (17th c.); afterwards a small chiefdom. Fill central Togo plateau Ewe chiefdoms with low confidence.

polities.name: Genyi
polities.note: Ga/Fante-derived (Guin) state at Little Popo on the Togo coast; German Togoland protectorate 1884.

polities.name: Kingdom of Allada
polities.note: Aja kingdom, parent of Dahomey and Porto-Novo dynasties; conquered by Dahomey 1724.

polities.name: Kingdom of Whydah
polities.note: Hueda coastal kingdom, major slave port at Ouidah; conquered by Dahomey 1727 (exiled Hueda raided from Grand-Popo afterwards).

polities.name: Kingdom of Dahomey
polities.note: Fon kingdom on the Abomey plateau; took Allada 1724 and Whydah 1727; Oyo tributary until Ghezo ended tribute 1823. French conquest 1892-94.

polities.name: Kingdom of Porto-Novo
polities.note: Gun/Aja kingdom founded by Allada princes; French protectorate 1863-64 and definitively 1882.

polities.name: Kingdom of Ketu
polities.note: Western Yoruba kingdom; sacked by Dahomey 1886, French 1894.

polities.name: Kingdom of Sabe
polities.note: Yoruba kingdom north of Dahomey; French 1894. Dassa and Shabe-Ijaluku nearby not itemised.

polities.name: Bussa
polities.note: Senior Borgu (Bariba) kingdom on the Niger; Mungo Park died at its rapids 1806. Old Bussa now under Kainji Lake. British (Royal Niger Company) 1898.

polities.name: Nikki
polities.note: Largest Borgu kingdom (cavalry state, Wasangari aristocracy) in NE Benin; Kandi, Kouandé, Parakou subordinate. French 1897.

polities.name: Tem chiefdoms
polities.note: Tem (Kotokoli) Muslim chiefdoms of central Togo under the Uro Esso of Tchaoudjo; German control 1898. Bassar and Kabye hills to the north largely stateless.

polities.name: Oyo Empire
polities.note: Exile at Igboho after Nupe sack (c.1535). Peak extent (c.1680-1790) includes Egbado corridor to the coast and Aja tributaries (Dahomey, Allada, Porto-Novo) - drawn polygon covers direct rule plus corridor. Ilorin revolt 1817-23; Oyo-Ile abandoned 1835-36.

polities.name: Oyo (Ago-Oyo)
polities.note: Rump Oyo kingdom re-founded by Alaafin Atiba south at Ago-Oyo; overshadowed by Ibadan. British bombardment 1895, protectorate 1896.

polities.name: Ife
polities.note: Sacred Yoruba city-kingdom of the Ooni; politically small after 1500; refugee Oyo settlement at Modakeke from 1840s. British protectorate c.1900.

polities.name: Ijebu Kingdom
polities.note: Yoruba kingdom of the Awujale controlling trade routes from Lagos lagoon to the interior; British punitive expedition 1892.

polities.name: Egba
polities.note: Egba townships refounded at Abeokuta c.1830 after the Owu war; earlier Egba forest towns (Orile Egba) were Oyo dependencies to the 1790s. Independence recognised 1893, ended 1914.

polities.name: Ibadan
polities.note: War-camp city-state that stopped the Fulani at Osogbo 1840 and dominated Ijesha, Ekiti and Osun towns until the Kiriji war (1877-86); British treaty 1893.

polities.name: Ijesha
polities.note: Yoruba kingdom of the Owa Obokun; led the Ekitiparapo against Ibadan.

polities.name: Ekiti kingdoms
polities.note: Cluster of ~16 Yoruba kingdoms (Ado, Ikere, Akure nearby, Otun, Ijero...) federated as Ekitiparapo 1877-86.

polities.name: Ondo Kingdom
polities.note: Yoruba kingdom of the Osemawe; British protectorate c.1899.

polities.name: Owo Kingdom
polities.note: Eastern Yoruba kingdom of the Olowo with strong Benin ties.

polities.name: Ilorin Emirate
polities.note: Former Oyo war camp under Afonja, taken over by Fulani; southernmost Sokoto emirate. Royal Niger Company conquest 1897.

polities.name: Kingdom of Lagos
polities.note: Island kingdom under Benin suzerainty; British bombardment 1851, annexation 1861 (Lagos Colony).

polities.name: Kingdom of Benin
polities.note: Expansion under Oba Ewuare (1440s) and successors to Lagos lagoon in the west and the Niger in the east (Onitsha, Agbor tributaries). British punitive expedition 1897.

polities.name: Warri Kingdom
polities.note: Itsekiri kingdom of the western Niger delta creeks; Catholic rulers 17th c.; interregnum from 1848 (governors of the river like Nana Olomu). British protectorate 1884.

polities.name: Onitsha
polities.note: Igbo kingdom of Benin-derived dynasty on the Niger east bank; British (Royal Niger Company) influence from 1857, protectorate c.1900.

polities.name: Aboh Kingdom
polities.note: Riverine Igbo trading kingdom at the head of the Niger delta; controlled river traffic until the 1860s.

polities.name: Igala Kingdom
polities.note: Kingdom of the Attah at the Niger-Benue confluence (south bank); fought Benin 1515-16; Royal Niger Company control 1890s-1900.

polities.name: Nupe Kingdom
polities.note: Founded by Tsoede on the middle Niger; sacked Oyo c.1535. Fulani dynasty from 1830s (emirate). Royal Niger Company conquest 1897, protectorate 1901. Gbara and Raba seats approximate.

polities.name: Kwararafa
polities.note: Multiethnic Benue valley confederacy that raided Kano, Katsina, Zazzau and sacked Ngazargamu (1680); declined in 18th c.; Jukun kingdom of Wukari as successor. British control c.1900.

polities.name: Aro Confederacy
polities.note: Igbo/Ibibio oracle-and-trade network centred on the Ibini Ukpabi shrine; 'extent' is the sphere of Aro colonies and influence over otherwise autonomous Igbo village-groups, not administered territory. Destroyed by the Anglo-Aro War 1901-02.

polities.name: Kingdom of Nri
polities.note: Igbo priest-kingdom with ritual rather than military hegemony; political reach mostly limited to Nri and nearby towns after 1700. British ended it 1911.

polities.name: Kingdom of Bonny
polities.note: Ijaw trading city-state, leading slave then palm-oil port; split 1869 when Jaja founded Opobo. British protectorate 1884.

polities.name: Kalabari Kingdom
polities.note: Ijaw city-state of the Amanyanabo; capital moved to Buguma 1884 after civil war. British protectorate 1884.

polities.name: Nembe Kingdom
polities.note: Ijaw kingdom of the Brass river; Akassa raid 1895 against the Royal Niger Company. Oil Rivers Protectorate 1884.

polities.name: Okrika Kingdom
polities.note: Small Ijaw island city-state between Bonny and Kalabari.

polities.name: Opobo
polities.note: Founded by Jaja after the Bonny civil war; controlled the Imo river palm-oil trade; Jaja deported by Britain 1887.

polities.name: Old Calabar
polities.note: Efik trading towns (Duke Town, Creek Town, Old Town) on the Calabar river under the Ekpe society; British protectorate 1884. Ibibio and Ekoi hinterland largely stateless.

polities.name: Sultanate of Kano
polities.note: Hausa state centred on walled Kano; absorbed Rano and parts of Biram; conquered by Fulani jihadists 1805-07 (see Kano Emirate).

polities.name: Sultanate of Katsina
polities.note: Hausa trading kingdom; Fulani jihad took Katsina 1807; the Hausa dynasty retreated to Maradi.

polities.name: Zazzau
polities.note: Southern Hausa kingdom (Queen Amina, 16th c.), slave-raiding frontier to the south; capital at Zaria from 1536. Fulani conquest 1808; Hausa dynasty withdrew to Abuja (Zuba).

polities.name: Gobir
polities.note: Northernmost Hausa state, moved south from Air under Tuareg pressure; destroyed Zamfara's capital 1756/62; fell to Uthman dan Fodio 1808. Birnin Lalle and Alkalawa positions approximate (~0.2 deg).

polities.name: Gobir (Tibiri)
polities.note: Independent rump Gobir north of Sokoto territory, allied with Maradi against the Caliphate; French control c.1900.

polities.name: Kingdom of Kebbi
polities.note: Founded by Kanta Kotal after breaking with Songhai; dominant in western Hausaland in 16th c. Fulani took Birnin Kebbi 1805; Kebbi resistance relocated to Argungu.

polities.name: Argungu
polities.note: Kebbi successor state that resisted Sokoto/Gwandu throughout the 19th c.; British 1903.

polities.name: Zamfara
polities.note: Hausa state; extent at height from Sabon Birni (N) to Kwiambana (S). Threw off Kebbi c.1715; Birnin Zamfara destroyed by Gobir c.1756/62, court fled to Kiawa; absorbed by Sokoto in the jihad (rump at Anka). Seats approximate.

polities.name: Daura
polities.note: Legendary senior Hausa state (Bayajidda); Fulani emirate from 1805 while the Hausa line ruled at Zango/Baure. Small territory.

polities.name: Yauri
polities.note: Hausa-Reshe kingdom on the Niger rapids; Muslim Hausa dynasty kept power as an emirate under Gwandu.

polities.name: Abuja (Zazzau)
polities.note: Hausa Zazzau dynasty refuge founded by Abu Ja after the Fulani took Zaria; independent of Sokoto; British 1902.

polities.name: Maradi
polities.note: Hausa Katsina dynasty in exile, raiding Sokoto territory; French control 1899-1900.

polities.name: Adar
polities.note: Hausa-Tuareg sultanate in the Tahoua region founded from Agadez; French 1900.

polities.name: Sokoto Caliphate
polities.note: Umbrella over ~30 emirates (draw constituent emirates on top). Sokoto ruled the eastern emirates; Gwandu the western (Nupe, Ilorin, Liptako, Yauri). Seat Sokoto from 1809 (earlier mobile/Sifawa). British conquest 1903.

polities.name: Gwandu Emirate
polities.note: Western half of the caliphate under Abdullahi dan Fodio and successors; overlord of Nupe, Ilorin, Yauri, Liptako, Kontagora (drawn separately). Polygon = Gwandu home territory.

polities.name: Kano Emirate
polities.note: Richest emirate of the caliphate; civil war 1893-95; British capture 1903.

polities.name: Katsina Emirate
polities.note: Fulani emirate replacing Hausa Katsina (whose dynasty held Maradi to the north).

polities.name: Zaria Emirate
polities.note: Fulani emirate of Zazzau; southern dependencies (Keffi, Jema'a, Nasarawa) raided the Middle Belt. British 1902-03.

polities.name: Bauchi Emirate
polities.note: Founded by Yakubu, the only non-Fulani flag-bearer; Bauchi town founded 1809. Jos Plateau peoples unconquered.

polities.name: Gombe Emirate
polities.note: Founded by Buba Yero; seat at Gombe Abba until 1840s, then Gombe (Doma).

polities.name: Katagum Emirate
polities.note: Frontier emirate facing Bornu; Misau and Jama'are emirates nearby (not itemised).

polities.name: Hadejia Emirate
polities.note: On the site of the Hausa state of Biram; rebellious under Buhari (1848-63). British 1906.

polities.name: Kontagora Emirate
polities.note: Slave-raiding frontier emirate founded by Umaru Nagwamatse; British 1901.

polities.name: Muri Emirate
polities.note: Fulani emirate on the upper Benue amid Jukun lands; seat moved to Jalingo 1893. Seat approximate.

polities.name: Adamawa Emirate
polities.note: Largest emirate by area (Fombina): a federation of lamidates (Ngaoundéré, Tibati, Banyo, Rey Bouba nominally, Garoua, Maroua) over many unconquered hill peoples. British took Yola 1901; most of it became German Kamerun.

polities.name: Rey Bouba
polities.note: Highly autonomous Fulani lamidate on the Mayo Rey in northern Cameroon; German protectorate 1901.

polities.name: Lamidate of Ngaoundéré
polities.note: Fulani lamidate on the Adamawa plateau conquered from the Mbum; German 1901. Tibati and Banyo lamidates to the west not itemised.

polities.name: Kanem-Bornu Empire

seat.name: Mobile court west of Lake Chad

polities.note: Sayfawa dynasty refounded west of Lake Chad after leaving Kanem (c.1380); Ngazargamu capital c.1472-1809 (sacked by Fulani 1808). Al-Kanemi Shehus from 1814 (Sayfawa ended 1846). Peak under Idris Alooma (1564-96) also held Kanem and Kawar - not drawn. Overthrown by Rabih 1893. Ngazargamu coordinates approx ±0.2 deg.

polities.name: Rabih's state
polities.note: Sudanese warlord Rabih conquered Bagirmi (1892) and Bornu (1893), ruling from Dikwa; killed by the French at Kousseri 1900. Bornu Shehus restored at Dikwa/Maiduguri under colonial rule.

polities.name: Sultanate of Damagaram
polities.note: Kanuri-led vassal of Bornu that grew strong on trans-Saharan trade in the 19th c.; French conquest 1899.

polities.name: Mandara Kingdom
polities.note: Wandala kingdom at the foot of the Mandara mountains, Islamised 1715; fought Bornu and Adamawa Fulani. German Kamerun 1902. Seats approximate.

polities.name: Kotoko kingdom
polities.note: Walled Kotoko city-states on the lower Logone/Chari (Logone-Birni, Kousseri, Makari, Afadé, Gulfei), Sao successors; partitioned between Germany and France 1900.

polities.name: Kingdom of Baguirmi
polities.note: Edge of region (SE of Lake Chad, may duplicate a central-Africa list). French protectorate 1897.

polities.name: Pabir (Biu)
polities.note: Pabir kingdom on the Biu plateau between Bornu and the Mandara/Margi hill peoples; British 1902.

polities.name: French Senegal
polities.note: Saint-Louis (1659) and Gorée (1677/1817) trading posts; Faidherbe's expansion from 1854 (Waalo 1855, Futa 1859, Cayor 1886). Part of French West Africa 1895/1902.

polities.name: French Sudan
polities.note: Military territory advancing from Kayes/Bamako (1883) to Ségou 1890, Timbuktu 1894, Mossi 1896; extent shown c.1898. Overlaps protectorates listed separately.

polities.name: French Guinea
polities.note: Rivières du Sud coastal posts from 1882, colony 1891; interior (Futa Jallon, Samori lands) occupied 1896-98.

polities.name: French Côte d'Ivoire
polities.note: Coastal posts at Grand-Bassam and Assinie from 1843 (reach_km applies), colony 1893; effective control of the forest interior only after 1908-15.

polities.name: French Dahomey
polities.note: Colony formed after the conquest of Dahomey (1892-94), with Porto-Novo and Borgu.

polities.name: German Togoland
polities.note: German protectorate from the Nachtigal treaty 1884; interior (Yendi, Sansanne-Mango) occupied 1896-99.

polities.name: British Gambia
polities.note: St Mary's Island settlement 1816, Ceded Mile 1826, MacCarthy Island 1823; river-strip boundary 1889, protectorate over chiefdoms 1894.

polities.name: Portuguese Guinea
polities.note: Fortified trading posts (Cacheu 1588, Bissau 1687) under Cape Verde until 1879; borders fixed 1886, but interior pacified only 1912-15.

polities.name: Dutch Gold Coast
aliases: Nederlandse Bezittingen ter Kuste van Guinea
polities.note: Chain of forts (Elmina from 1637, Axim, Shama, Butre...); sold to Britain 1872. Draw as coastal points only.

polities.name: Danish Gold Coast
polities.note: Forts at Osu and east to Keta; sold to Britain 1850.

polities.name: Brandenburger Gold Coast
polities.note: Brandenburg-Prussian forts near Cape Three Points; sold to the Dutch 1717-21.

polities.name: British Gold Coast
polities.note: Forts (Cape Coast Castle) with an informal Fante protectorate (Bond of 1844); crown colony 1874 south of Asante; Asante annexed 1901, Northern Territories 1901.

polities.name: Lagos Colony
polities.note: Annexed 1861; Badagry, Epe and lagoon coast added 1863-1880s; Yoruba hinterland protectorate from 1893.

polities.name: Niger Coast Protectorate
polities.note: Oil Rivers Protectorate 1884, renamed 1893; treaty protectorate over Delta city-states; merged into Southern Nigeria 1900.

polities.name: Royal Niger Company territories
polities.note: Chartered company rule along the lower Niger and Benue (Asaba HQ; posts to Lokoja and Ibi); conquered Nupe and Ilorin 1897. Charter revoked 1900.

gaps.note: Largely stateless Jola villages and small Bainuk/Kasa chiefdoms; Kasa kingdom existed to c.1600 but no reliable extent. Leave unassigned or as Kaabu fringe.

gaps.area: Coastal Guinea-Bissau (Bijagos islands, Balanta, Manjak, Biafada lowlands)
gaps.note: Mostly stateless or small chiefdoms (Biafada Guinala kingdom 15th-17th c.; Bijagos island chiefs). Portuguese posts at Cacheu (1588) and Bissau (1687). Fill only with Portuguese Guinea after 1879.

gaps.area: Western Sahara interior north of Adrar (Tiris, Zemmour)
gaps.note: Nomadic Reguibat and Oulad Delim tribal ranges without an emirate; outside the settled emirates.

gaps.area: Guinea forest region and northern Liberia interior (Kissi, Kpelle, Loma/Toma, Mano, Dan)
gaps.note: Small chiefdoms and village federations without an overarching state; Samori raided 1880s-90s. Low-density forest; leave unfilled or mark as stateless.

gaps.area: Liberian interior (Gola, Bassa, Kru hinterland, Krahn)
gaps.note: Chiefdoms only; Liberian authority stopped near the coast until after 1900. Condo covers the NW only.

gaps.area: Coastal Guinea (Baga, Nalu, Landuma, Susu lowlands north of Conakry)
gaps.note: Small Susu/Baga/Nalu chiefdoms (e.g. Kaloum, Dubréka, Rio Nunez); not itemised; Futa Jallon held loose hegemony in 18th-19th c.

gaps.area: Gurunsi, Lobi, Dagara and Bwa country (southern Burkina Faso / NW Ghana)
gaps.note: Acephalous societies without states between Mossi, Wala, Gwiriko and Dagbon; raided by Zabarima warlords Babatu and Gazari (1860s-1890s). Leave stateless.
Nomadic ranges of Kunta and Berabich Arabs and Tuareg; no settled polity beyond Araouane/Taoudenni salt camps. Mostly uninhabited desert.

gaps.area: Ténéré and Erg of Bilma (NE Niger)
gaps.note: Uninhabited sand desert except the Kawar oases (Bilma, Djado) under Kanuri/Tubu chiefs and Bornu suzerainty.

gaps.area: Western Cote d'Ivoire forest (Kru, Bété, Dida, Guéré, Dan, Gouro)
gaps.note: Stateless lineage-based societies; no kingdoms. Leave unfilled (Kru coast entry covers only Liberian side).

gaps.area: Lagoon coast of Cote d'Ivoire (Abidjan lagoons: Ebrié, Adioukrou, Alladian, Avikam)
gaps.note: Village-federation 'lagoon peoples' without central rulers, between Sanwi and the Kru coast.

gaps.area: Volta basin east of Asante (Krachi, Nchumuru, Adele, Akposso)
gaps.note: Small chiefdoms and the Dente oracle shrine at Kete-Krachi; under loose Asante hegemony 1744-1874.

gaps.area: Western Niger Delta hinterland (Urhobo, Isoko, western Ijaw clans)
gaps.note: Clan polities without kingdoms (some small Urhobo kingdoms like Okpe); between Warri and Benin. Leave fragmented.

gaps.area: Togo-Benin Atakora and central Togo hills (Kabye, Bassar, Tamberma, Somba)
gaps.note: Largely stateless highland peoples between Tem chiefdoms, Nikki/Borgu and Dagbon; Bassar iron-working chiefdom tributary to Dagbon.

gaps.area: Igbo heartland and Ibibio/Annang country (SE Nigeria)
gaps.note: Thousands of autonomous village-groups; only Nri (ritual), Aro (trade network), Onitsha, Aboh and the Efik/Ijaw city-states had kings. The Aro extent is an influence zone - draw lightly or leave stateless.

gaps.area: Middle Belt plateau and Benue lowlands (Tiv, Idoma, Gwari, Jos Plateau peoples, Bachama)
gaps.note: Mostly stateless or small chiefdoms between Kwararafa/Jukun, Zazzau, Bauchi and Igala; Jos plateau refuge area never conquered by the emirates.

gaps.area: Mandara mountains and Alantika/Shebshi hills (Mafa, Kapsiki, Margi, Gudur, Fali, Bata)
gaps.note: Refuge hill peoples outside Mandara, Bornu and Adamawa control; small chiefdoms (Gudur ritual centre). Leave as unconquered enclaves inside Adamawa/Mandara.

gaps.area: Kanem (NE of Lake Chad) and Kawar oases
gaps.note: Bulala sultanate of Kanem (to c.1600) then Bornu/Wadai-contested Kanem chiefs and Tubu (Teda) nomads; probably belongs to a central Sahara/Chad list.

gaps.area: Southern Cameroon / Grassfields (Bamum, Bamileke, Tikar, Duala coast)
gaps.note: Outside the assigned northern-Cameroon scope; Bamum, Bamileke chiefdoms, Duala and German Kamerun (1884) should come from a central-Africa list.
